From 7b568e9eba2fad89a696f22f0413d44cf4a1f892 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Zide Chen <zide.chen@intel.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 10:40:48 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] perf/x86/intel/uncore: Skip discovery table for offline dies

This warning can be triggered if NUMA is disabled and the system
boots with fewer CPUs than the number of CPUs in die 0.

WARNING: CPU: 9 PID: 7257 at uncore.c:1157 uncore_pci_pmu_register+0x136/0x160 [intel_uncore]

Currently, the discovery table continues to be parsed even if all CPUs
in the associated die are offline.  This can lead to an array overflow
at "pmu->boxes[die] = box" in uncore_pci_pmu_register(), which may
trigger the warning above or cause other issues.

Fixes: edae1f06c2cd ("perf/x86/intel/uncore: Parse uncore discovery tables")
Reported-by: Steve Wahl <steve.wahl@hpe.com>
Signed-off-by: Zide Chen <zide.chen@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Reviewed-by: Dapeng Mi <dapeng1.mi@linux.intel.com>
Tested-by: Steve Wahl <steve.wahl@hpe.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260313174050.171704-3-zide.chen@intel.com

diff --git a/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.c b/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.c
index 427939be2fb4..583cbd06b9b8 100644
--- a/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.c
+++ b/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.c
@@ -371,7 +371,7 @@ static bool uncore_discovery_pci(struct uncore_discovery_domain *domain)
 				     (val & UNCORE_DISCOVERY_DVSEC2_BIR_MASK) * UNCORE_DISCOVERY_BIR_STEP;
 
 			die = get_device_die_id(dev);
-			if (die < 0)
+			if ((die < 0) || (die >= uncore_max_dies()))
 				continue;
 
 			parse_discovery_table(domain, dev, die, bar_offset, &parsed);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch Modifications

### File Modified: `arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.c`

- **Change in function `uncore_discovery_pci()`**:
  - The condition that checks the validity of the `die` index was expanded.
  - **Before**: `if (die < 0) continue;`
  - **After**: `if ((die < 0) || (die >= uncore_max_dies())) continue;`
  - This addition prevents processing of discovery table entries for die indices that exceed the number of available (online) dies, which could occur when NUMA is disabled and the system boots with fewer CPUs than those originally belonging to die 0.

### Relationship to the Bug

The bug was triggered when the system had offline dies (e.g., due to NUMA being disabled or reduced CPU count). The old check only rejected negative die indices, but valid but out-of-range positive indices (e.g., die 0 when it is offline) would still be processed. This led to an array overflow in `uncore_pci_pmu_register()` at `pmu->boxes[die] = box`, causing a kernel warning or other undefined behavior.

The fix ensures that any die index that is not within the actual die count (based on online dies) is skipped entirely, preventing the overflow and the associated warning.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
`die = get_device_die_id(dev);`
`if (die < 0)`
`    continue;`
Reason:
This code only checks for negative die IDs, but does not validate that `die` is within the range of online dies (`die >= uncore_max_dies()`). When dies are offline (e.g., due to NUMA being disabled or fewer CPUs booted), `get_device_die_id()` can return a valid but out‑of‑range die index. This index is later used in `uncore_pci_pmu_register()` to access `pmu->boxes[die]`, causing an array overflow and triggering the warning.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`if ((die < 0) || (die >= uncore_max_dies()))`
`    continue;`
Reason:
By adding the condition `die >= uncore_max_dies()`, the code now skips any die that is not present in the current online set. This prevents out‑of‑range indices from being passed to `parse_discovery_table()` and avoids the array overflow in `uncore_pci_pmu_register()`.
